system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: each step encompassing access to a screenshot of the current UI and a dynamically generated document detailing the functions of UI elements
system_prompt_style.note: Only file names (scripts/prompts.py) visible; the prompt code itself is not in the evidence. Coded from paper prose.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The agent receives two key inputs: a real-time screenshot showing the app's interface and an XML file detailing the interactive elements.
env_context_strategy.note: Screen state and XML are injected every step, together with the document base generated during exploration. The agent can also navigate the app with actions.

context_compaction.note: The paper says the agent summarizes history into the next prompt. Code for the history handling (task_executor.py) is not included in the evidence.

observation_format.evidence_quote: These elements are overlaid as semi-transparent numbers on the screenshot.
observation_format.note: Changelog lists an optional grid overlay. XML is used to build the labels.

tool_call_format.note: The model writes function-call text (tap(5)) that is parsed out of its response. Closest value is code_as_action. The parser is not in the evidence.

tool_count.note: The paper lists tap, long_press, swipe, text, back and exit, which is 6 functions despite the text saying four. The optional grid action is not counted.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Our agent's action space mirrors common human interactions with smartphones: taps and swipes.
edit_primitive.note: GUI action space only; there is no file-editing tool.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: The prompts also provide detailed explanations of all available actions.

protocol_standardization.note: Source and dependency contents are not included in the evidence (only requirements.txt filename).

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the agent is first tasked with providing its observations of the current UI, followed by articulating its thought process concerning the task and current observations. Subsequently, the agent proceeds to execute actions
loop_primitives.note: The exploration phase (learn.py) adds reflection and document generation.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: followed by articulating its thought process concerning the task and current observations

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: the agent proceeds to execute actions by invoking available functions

delegation_mechanism.note: The run loop code is not in the evidence.

human_in_loop.note: Human demonstration mode exists, but it is a learning input and not HITL gating. The run loop code is not in the evidence.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the agent summarizes the interaction history and the actions taken during the current step. This information is incorporated into the next prompt

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: the agent generates documentation for elements interacted during the exploration/demonstration and saves them for use in the deployment phase.
long_term_memory.note: The per-app UI element documentation base is persisted and reused across runs.

state_persistence.note: Code is not in the evidence.

self_verification.evidence_quote: AppAgent will reflect on its previous action making sure its action adheres to the given task
self_verification.note: Reflection happens in the autonomous exploration mode.

retry_policy.note: Code is not in the evidence.

rollback.note: Back() is a GUI navigation action, not rollback. Code is not in the evidence.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: For the exploration phase, we capped the maximum number of steps at 40. During testing, we limited the maximum number of steps to 10.
termination_condition.note: The model declares completion with Exit() (paper Sec. 3.3). A config field for max rounds is likely in config.yaml, but its contents are not shown.

cost_controls.note: The config.yaml contents are not in the evidence. The request interval is only a rate limit.

timeouts.note: Code is not in the evidence.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote:
download and install [Android Debug Bridge](https://developer.android.com/tools/adb) (adb) which is a
command-line tool that lets you communicate with your Android device from the PC.
execution_isolation.note: Actions run on a separate Android device or emulator via adb. Closest value is remote; vm is also plausible for the emulator.

filesystem_access.note: The action space is GUI-only, so filesystem access is not applicable or reported.

network_policy.note: Code and config contents are not in the evidence.

permission_model.note: Code is not in the evidence.

tracing.note: Code is not in the evidence.

replayability.note: Code is not in the evidence.

eval_hooks.note: The file tree has only a markdown test set and no evaluation runner.

guardrails.note: Code is not in the evidence.

target_domain.evidence_quote: an LLM-based multimodal agent framework designed to operate smartphone apps.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: If you want to test AppAgent using your own models, you should write a new model class in `scripts/model.py` accordingly.
model_agnostic.note: Ships OpenAI and Qwen options behind a model class abstraction; there is no litellm.

first_release_date.note: Based on the open-source date in the changelog. No tag information was available.
